proposals.before: Soldier households that were wealthy merchants supplied an additional man as a surplus-male soldier, exempted after fifteen years of service.
proposals.after: Soldier households that were wealthy merchants supplied an additional man as a surplus-male soldier; they were exempted in the fifteenth year.
proposals.reason: Chinese 至十五年免, following 至元七年, most naturally marks exemption in the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan, not a fifteen-year term of service.

proposals.before: [County] darughachi Hu Yu; Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Binzhou with 100 soldiers; the Haikou darughachi Talahai of Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and fifty-five others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; and Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.
proposals.after: [County] darughachi Hu Yu; Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Bindizhou with 100 soldiers; the Haikou darughachi Talahai of Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and fifty-five others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; and Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 濱棣州 names Bin and Di prefectures together, not Binzhou alone.

proposals.before: [County] darughachi Hu Yu, Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Binzhou with 100 soldiers; darughachi Talahai of Haikou in Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and 55 others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.
proposals.after: [County] darughachi Hu Yu, Commander of a Thousand Households Wang Duanchen with 704 soldiers; Commander of a Thousand Households Wolai of Baliushu with 361 soldiers; Pangchao'erchi and Zhang Xin of Mengzhou with 190 soldiers; Chief Captain Zhang Shan of Haikou in Bindizhou with 100 soldiers; darughachi Talahai of Haikou in Cangzhou with 100 soldiers; Meng Chun and 55 others under Chief Administrator Li of Suizhou; Commander of Ten Thousand Households Xiao of Bazhou with 195 soldiers—all obeyed his command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 濱棣州 names Bin and Di prefectures together, not Binzhou alone.

proposals.before: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "The soldiers garrisoning Jinchuan—their home ordu have already served; they are now doubly overburdened."
proposals.after: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "The soldiers garrisoning Jinzhou—their home ordu have already served; they are now doubly overburdened."
proposals.reason: 金州 is Jinzhou, not Jinchuan.

proposals.before: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "Soldiers garrisoning Jinchuan—the various ordu have already served; now they are doubly burdened and toiled."
proposals.after: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "Soldiers garrisoning Jinzhou—the various ordu have already served; now they are doubly burdened and toiled."
proposals.reason: 金州 is Jinzhou, not Jinchuan.

proposals.before: Even commanders with fewer than five hundred troops, if their families were wealthy and their sons robust, also supplied one tulughachi with the same horses, oxen, and farmers.
proposals.after: Even commanders with fewer than five hundred troops, if their families were wealthy and strong and their sons and younger brothers robust, also supplied one tulughachi with the same horses, oxen, and farmers.
proposals.reason: Chinese 家富強子弟健壯者 marks the household as wealthy and strong and 子弟 as sons and younger brothers, which the idiomatic line reduces to sons alone.

proposals.before: Sons serving as tulughachi brought their wives and children; attendants were unlimited; horses and oxen beyond the stipulated quota were permitted.
proposals.after: Sons and younger brothers of commanders of ten thousand and of a thousand households who served as tulughachi brought their wives and children with them; attendants were not limited to a fixed number; horses and oxen beyond the stipulated quota were permitted.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence drops 萬戶、千戶子弟 and compresses 從人不拘定數, omitting whose sons served and that attendants had no fixed quota.

proposals.before: That month the Emperor restored Taizong's practice of separate offices for military and civilian administration.
proposals.after: That month the Emperor, following Taizong's former institutions, established officials and divided duties so that military and civilian affairs each had their own charge.
proposals.reason: 以 means following or using Taizong's old institutions, not necessarily restoring them; 設官分職 is establishing officials and dividing duties.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month, provincial and central officials decided that 3,804 persons caught smuggling horses along secret routes and crossing the southern border would all be conscripted—1,978 to the Shandong Army Command, 1,000 to the Caizhou commander of ten thousand households; the remaining 826 households were ordered kept in military service.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month, provincial and central officials decided that 3,804 households received for privately traveling bypaths, illicitly trading horses, and having crossed the southern border would all be made to serve as soldiers—1,978 men to the Shandong Army Command, 1,000 to the Caizhou commander of ten thousand households; the remaining 826 households were ordered kept in military service.
proposals.reason: Opening 三千八百四戶 counts households, not persons; the idiomatic line converts that census unit to persons while later reverting to households.

proposals.before: In the second month, officials were sent to draft soldiers from Pingyang and Taiyuan. Exempt were military, relay, monastic, Nestorian, Muslim, and Confucian households; from government, appanage, transport, artisan, hunting, mining, and similar households—regardless of category—two thousand men were selected from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, organized under commanders of a hundred households and platoon heads, and sent to campaign in Eastern Chuan under the Shaanxi-Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
proposals.after: In the second month, officials were sent to draft soldiers from Pingyang and Taiyuan. Exempt were military, relay, monastic, Daoist, Nestorian, Muslim, and Confucian households; from government, appanage, transport, artisan, hunting, mining, and similar households—regardless of category—two thousand men were selected from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, organized under commanders of a hundred households and platoon heads, and sent to campaign in Eastern Chuan under the Shaanxi-Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Chinese lists 僧 and 道 separately; the idiomatic rendering folds Daoists into monastic and omits 道.

proposals.before: In the fifth month, an edict declared: "In the Henan Circuit, select 420 soldiers from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, assign them to the Bureau of Military Affairs for campaign, and restore their corvée obligations.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, an edict declared: "In the Henan Circuit, select 420 soldiers from middle households with the most able-bodied sons, assign them to the Bureau of Military Affairs for campaign, and remit their corvée obligations.
proposals.reason: 復其徭役 in this military-household context means to exempt or remit corvée, not to restore labor duties.

proposals.before: Fifth month, an edict: "In the Henan Circuit, from middle households selecting those with many adult males fit for military households, 420 soldiers are to be conscripted, assigned to the Bureau of Military Affairs, made to serve in the armies, and their corvée restored.
proposals.after: Fifth month, an edict: "In the Henan Circuit, from middle households selecting those with many adult males fit for military households, 420 soldiers are to be conscripted, assigned to the Bureau of Military Affairs, made to serve in the armies, and their corvée remitted.
proposals.reason: Literal corvée restored reverses 復其徭役, which here remits corvée for conscripted military households.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month, three thousand Jurchen and Suichen troops were conscripted.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month, three thousand Jurchen and Water Tatar troops were conscripted.
proposals.reason: 水達達 is the Water Tatars, not a name Suichen.

proposals.before: Twelfth month: three thousand Jurchen and Suichen troops were conscripted.
proposals.after: Twelfth month: three thousand Jurchen and Water Tatar troops were conscripted.
proposals.reason: 水達達 should be rendered Water Tatars; Suichen is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: In the sixth month, provincial ministers recommended: "Among tulughachi previously conscripted, many officers have been transferred, died, or dismissed, leaving poor Mongols in hardship. Only darughachi, chief administrators, and commanders of ten thousand households should remain obliged; other officials' tulughachi should be released, though those who wish to stay as hostages may do so."
proposals.after: In the sixth month, provincial ministers recommended: "Among tulugha previously conscripted, many officers have been transferred, died, or dismissed, leaving poor Mongols in hardship. Only darughachi, chief administrators, and commanders of ten thousand households should remain obliged; other officials' tulugha should be released, though those who wish to stay as hostages may do so."
proposals.reason: 禿魯花 are tulugha hostage-sons, not tulughachi; the -chi suffix confuses the term with an official title.

proposals.before: Sixth month: provincial ministers deliberated: "Tulughachi officials who were conscripted have all been transferred, or died or were dismissed; among them are again poor and distressed Mongol persons. Apart from the darughachi, chief administrators, and military commanders of ten thousand households of each circuit's general administration, who ought to fulfill their obligation, tulughachi of other officials should be released; those who voluntarily remain as hostages may do so."
proposals.after: Sixth month: provincial ministers deliberated: "Tulugha who were conscripted as officials' hostages have all been transferred, or died or were dismissed; among them are again poor and distressed Mongol persons. Apart from the darughachi, chief administrators, and military commanders of ten thousand households of each circuit's general administration, who ought to fulfill their obligation, tulugha of other officials should be released; those who voluntarily remain as hostages may do so."
proposals.reason: The source is 禿魯花 hostage retainers of officials, not an office titled tulughachi.

proposals.before: At the beginning, when the Grand Ancestor and Taizong undertook campaigns, [troops] were levied from the various circuits; when prefectures and counties were captured, iron, wood, metal, fire, and other artisans were recruited as artillerymen and led on campaign; in the renyi year all were registered as artillery households.
proposals.after: At the beginning, when the Grand Ancestor and Taizong undertook campaigns, [troops] were levied from the various circuits; when prefectures and counties were captured, iron, wood, metal, fire, and other artisans were recruited as artillerymen and led on campaign; in the renzi year all were registered as artillery households.
proposals.reason: 壬子 is the renzi sexagenary year, not renyi.

proposals.before: In the sixth month, Li Xun, chief of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Because of recent conscription, we ask to follow the Xu and Pizhou precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls and two pay grain tax. We can draft over seven hundred able-bodied men plus the assigned baojia men, place them under my command to garrison Yingzhou, replace present colony grain payments, and supply war horses separately."
proposals.after: In the sixth month, Li Xun, chief of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Because of recent conscription, we ask to follow the Xu and Pizhou precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls and two pay grain tax. We can draft over seven hundred able-bodied men plus the assigned baojia men, place them under my command to garrison Yingzhou, and release the presently stationed troops and horses of Nahe, the battle supervisor, for other use."
proposals.reason: Chinese 代見屯納合監戰軍馬別用 names 納合 as battle supervisor and asks that his presently garrisoned troops and horses be put to other use; the idiomatic English dropped the personal name and recast the clause as grain payments and separately supplied war horses.

proposals.before: Sixth month: Li Xun, chief administrator of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Recently because of conscription affairs, we beg to follow the Xu and Pizhou military-colony precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls, two pay grain tax—we can conscript over seven hundred able-bodied men, together with the originally assigned baojia able-bodied men, place them all under Xun's command to garrison Yingzhou, replacing the present colony grain payments and separately supplying war horses for the supervisor."
proposals.after: Sixth month: Li Xun, chief administrator of the Yingzhou military colony, reported: "Recently because of conscription affairs, we beg to follow the Xu and Pizhou military-colony precedent: of every three adult males, one garrisons the walls, two pay grain tax—we can conscript over seven hundred able-bodied men, together with the originally assigned baojia able-bodied men, place them all under Xun's command to garrison Yingzhou, replacing the presently stationed troops and horses of Nahe, the battle supervisor, for other use."
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise turns 納合監戰軍馬 into unnamed grain payments and horses for a supervisor, omitting the personal name 納合 and the sense of substituting that garrison.

proposals.before: In the fifth month, Liu Fuheng, the Zhengyang commander of ten thousand households, reported: "Over thirty newly taken Jiangnan cities are all under garrison. With north-of-the-River, Huainan, Runzhou, and Yangzhou still unredeemed, our forces are spread thin and supplies cannot keep pace, and Zhenchao Army and Chuzhou have rebelled again.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, Liu Fuheng, the Zhengyang commander of ten thousand households, reported: "Over thirty newly taken Jiangnan cities are all under garrison. With north-of-the-River, Huainan, Runzhou, and Yangzhou still unsurrendered, our forces are spread thin and supplies cannot keep pace, and Zhenchao Army and Chuzhou have rebelled again.
proposals.reason: 未降 means the places had not yet surrendered; "unredeemed" misstates the military-political situation.

proposals.before: In the first month of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered: "Two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be drafted from registered civilian and hunting households in the Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Bejing circuits to garrison Shangdu."
proposals.after: In the first month of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered: "Two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be drafted from registered civilian and hunting households in the Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Beijing circuits to garrison Shangdu."
proposals.reason: English misspells 北京 as Bejing.

proposals.before: Fourteenth year, first month, an edict: "From registered civilian hunting and other households of the four circuits of Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Bejing, two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be conscripted and selected to garrison Shangdu."
proposals.after: Fourteenth year, first month, an edict: "From registered civilian hunting and other households of the four circuits of Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and Beijing, two thousand able-bodied soldiers are to be conscripted and selected to garrison Shangdu."
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the Bejing misspelling of 北京.

proposals.before: Now the ordu chief administrators of Dongping and other circuits report that deaths and depleted estates often leave households unable to supply two soldiers, and ask that surplus-adult service be waived."
proposals.after: Now the aolu (military-household base) chief administrators of Dongping and other circuits report that deaths and depleted estates often leave households unable to supply two soldiers, and ask that surplus-adult service be waived."
proposals.reason: 奧魯 is the aolu/a'uruq military-household base, not ordu.

proposals.before: Before the Southern Song was pacified, Mongols and men of every category who had offended fled north to join them. Now the realm is settled, yet they still hide in the wilds.
proposals.after: Before the Southern Song was pacified, Mongols and men of every category who had offended fled as outlaws to take refuge with them. Now the realm is settled, yet they still hide in the wilds.
proposals.reason: 亡命往依焉 is flight to take refuge with still-unpacified Southern Song; "fled north" reverses the geography.

proposals.before: An edict exempted them, and also issued an edict the officials not to impose heavy corvée on military households.
proposals.after: An edict exempted them, and also issued an edict that officials were not to impose heavy corvée on military households.
proposals.reason: Literal English omits a complementizer after “edict,” yielding an ungrammatical clause that obscures the second imperial order.

proposals.before: The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat recruited salt convicts as soldiers, obtaining four thousand seven hundred sixty-six men; military officers under command with no troops were selected to jointly command them, to prepare for garrison duty in various places.
proposals.after: The Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat recruited salt convicts as soldiers, obtaining four thousand seven hundred sixty-six men; military officers who had no soldiers under their command were selected to jointly command them, to prepare for garrison duty in various places.
proposals.reason: 麾下無士卒者 means officers who had no troops under them, not “officers under command.”

proposals.before: Originally the four hundred households of Limaoge and others had belonged to Prince Toto; in the yimi year they were registered as civilians, but during the Koryo Lin Yan and Nayan rebellions they had all been conscripted.
proposals.after: Originally the four hundred households of Limaoge and others had belonged to Prince Toto; in the yiwei year they were registered as civilians, but during the rebellions of Lin Yan of Koryo and of Nayan they had all been conscripted.
proposals.reason: 乙未 is yiwei, not yimi; 高麗林衍 is Lin Yan of Koryo, not a fused personal name Koryo Lin Yan.

proposals.before: Initially, the four hundred households of Limaoge and others belonged to the princely lord Toto; in the yimi year they were fixed in the register as civilians; when the Koryo Lin Yan and Nayan rebelled, they were all once conscripted as soldiers.
proposals.after: Initially, the four hundred households of Limaoge and others belonged to the princely lord Toto; in the yiwei year they were fixed in the register as civilians; when Lin Yan of Koryo and Nayan rebelled, they were all once conscripted as soldiers.
proposals.reason: 乙未 is yiwei; 高麗 modifies Lin Yan's polity, not a compound given name.

proposals.before: On this occasion provincial officials raised the issue, and an order directed that the register fixed in the yimi year be followed.
proposals.after: On this occasion provincial officials raised the issue, and an order directed that the register fixed in the yiwei year be followed.
proposals.reason: 乙未年 is the yiwei-year register, not yimi.

proposals.before: At this point provincial officials spoke on the matter; an order directed following the register fixed in the yimi year.
proposals.after: At this point provincial officials spoke on the matter; an order directed following the register fixed in the yiwei year.
proposals.reason: 乙未年 is yiwei, not yimi.

proposals.after: Maiju and Nangjiadai were appointed to command the left and right divisions respectively.

proposals.before: Buyiju and Nangjiadai were again ordered to command them in left and right divisions.
proposals.after: Maiju and Nangjiadai were again ordered to command them in left and right divisions.
proposals.reason: 買住 is Maiju/Maizhu; the English Buyiju does not match the Chinese.

The literal likewise misrenders 金州 as Jinchuan; Jinzhou is the correct toponym.
